evidence_points: The run accepted the Act 1 floor 3 event for 16 HP, dropping from 80 to 64.
It then accepted the Act 1 floor 4 Gather Gold option for another 11 HP, and later reached the floor 13 event at 63 HP before ending that sequence at 33 HP.
By Act 2 floor 27 the run was at 8 HP, and although it rested to 32, it reached the final fight with only 10 HP.
reasoning: Each individual HP payment was survivable, but the accumulated losses reduced the margin for ordinary Act 2 combats and left no buffer for the final elite fight. Future decisions should value a stable HP trajectory over small optional rewards when several costs are being considered in succession.

title: Use live attack-intent strength before setting up slow block
situation: When several enemies are attacking and Spot Weakness+ is legal, especially alongside a high-impact card such as Fiend Fire, prioritize the immediate strength gain unless the alternative clearly prevents lethal damage.
lesson: In the final fight, after Battle Trance revealed Spot Weakness+, do not spend the next energy on Metallicize by default; consider Spot Weakness+ first, then allocate the remaining energy to the best available combination of block and damage.
evidence_points: After Battle Trance on turn 2, the character had 4 energy and Spot Weakness+ was legal against all three enemies.
Both Mad Gremlins and the Gremlin Leader had attack intents at that decision.
The chosen sequence played Metallicize, Defend, and Fiend Fire, leaving Spot Weakness+ unused.
reasoning: Spot Weakness+ was immediately enabled by the logged attack intents and could improve the current Fiend Fire and later attacks. Metallicize provided delayed value while the character was already at 17 HP with no block, so this sequencing likely sacrificed immediate damage or defensive efficiency; the exact optimal line is somewhat uncertain because incoming damage values are not logged.

title: Stop escalating HP-for-relic gambles
situation: When an event offers repeated increasingly costly attempts with uncertain relic rewards, especially before several upcoming combats.
lesson: Set a risk limit before taking the first attempt; after spending several HP without a reward, leave rather than continuing to pay for another low-probability roll.
evidence_points: At Act 1 Floor 5, the run chose Reach Inside and then Deeper twice, losing 3, 4, and 5 HP in succession, ending at 59/78 HP.
Immediately afterward, the run used a Blood Potion, and the final relic list contains no relic from that event.
reasoning: The sequence converted 12 HP and a potion into no recorded relic gain, increasing vulnerability before later fights. A predefined stopping point would preserve HP and resources when the early attempts fail.

title: Against a near-lethal attack, evaluate the damage-first line before blocking
situation: When HP is critically low, the enemy is near death, and a zero-cost draw or strength card can precede an attack.
lesson: Before spending energy on a small block, compare whether draw-plus-buff-plus-attack can end or substantially shorten the fight; do not automatically use the first available defensive card.
evidence_points: On Turn 8 at 11/87 HP against the Chosen at 31 HP with an attack intent, Feed+, Limit Break+, and Battle Trance+ were all legal before Shrug It Off was played.
After playing Shrug It Off, Battle Trance+, and Uppercut+, the Chosen was still alive at 16 HP, and the run ended the turn with Flex+ still legal.
Earlier, at 29/87 HP against an attacking Chosen, Uppercut+ was chosen while Defend and Shockwave were legal; a later decision then used Defend with only 1 energy remaining.
reasoning: The exact counterfactual outcome cannot be recovered, but the logged alternatives show that energy ordering mattered. In low-HP races, spending energy on a small block or attacking before using available draw/buffs can leave the enemy alive for another dangerous turn.

title: Repeat the early Feed investment
situation: When Feed is available early and the deck can reliably create finishing opportunities.
lesson: Prioritize taking Feed early, upgrade it when practical, and deliberately preserve opportunities to finish weakened enemies with it rather than using it as ordinary damage.
evidence_points: Feed was selected from the initial rare-card offer and later upgraded at Act 1 Floor 15.
The combat logs show Feed finishing enemies including a Louse, Spike Slime, Gremlin Nob, Jaw Worm, Slaver, and Looter.
The final build contains Feed+, and maximum HP increased from 72 at the initial reward state to 87 entering Act 2.
reasoning: This was one of the run's clearest successful, repeatable strategies: early acquisition plus upgrading converted routine kills into persistent survivability and helped compensate for the deck's later attrition.

title: At critical HP, prioritize immediate survival over setup
situation: When HP is low and an enemy is attacking, especially in a multi-enemy fight, compare every damage or setup play against the strongest available block option.
lesson: Do not spend a low-HP turn on Rage or other non-defensive setup while an attack is incoming. In this state, play the legal Power Through or otherwise maximize immediate mitigation before pursuing damage.
evidence_points: On turn 3 of the Sentry fight, the player had 12/80 HP, the middle Sentry had Intent ATTACK, and Power Through was a legal alternative.
The chosen sequence was Play Rage, Play Pummel, Play Defend, Play Defend, then End turn; Power Through was still legal immediately before ending the turn.
The run died in the following Sentry combat, with the final logged state still showing three Sentries alive.
reasoning: The logged state explicitly presents an attacking enemy and a playable defensive card at critical HP. Although exact incoming damage is unavailable, choosing setup and then ending without Power Through gave up a clear survival opportunity.

title: After a damaging elite fight, healing can be worth more than a second upgrade
situation: At a campfire after an elite or other costly combat, when below full HP and several Act 1 fights remain, favor recovery unless the upgrade is essential to survive a known upcoming fight.
lesson: Reassess smithing at moderate or low HP instead of upgrading automatically. Preserving a larger HP buffer can be more valuable than improving a card when the route still contains multiple combats.
evidence_points: After the Lagavulin combat ended at 53/80 HP, the next campfire at floor 8 showed both rest and smith as legal alternatives.
The agent chose smith and upgraded Disarm while remaining at 59/80 HP, rather than restoring HP.
The next logged combats reduced HP to 23/80 after the Acid Slime/Slaver fight, then to 20/80 after the Looter fight, before the fatal Sentry combat.
reasoning: The run had already paid a substantial HP cost for the elite and then continued through several combats without a healing choice. The later HP collapse shows that maintaining a buffer was important, though the exact counterfactual benefit of resting cannot be proven.

title: At low HP, prioritize immediate defense over nonlethal damage
situation: When entering a fight at low HP and the hand contains legal block cards, especially against multiple enemies, use defense unless the attack clearly secures a kill.
lesson: Do not spend the opening turn on Whirlwind or another broad attack merely for damage when survival is uncertain. In the final fight, choose a Defend line first because the enemies were still substantially alive and two Defends were legal.
evidence_points: Turn 1 began at 38/80 HP with 0 Block; the hand contained two Defends, while Whirlwind+ was selected.
Turn 2 began at 20/80 HP with 0 Block, and Shelled Parasite still had 54/72 HP while Fungi Beast still had 25/25 HP.
The final combat summary records Whirlwind+ followed by Defend, Bash+, and Wild Strike, ending the logged sequence at only 20/80 HP.
reasoning: The chosen attack did not immediately resolve either enemy, and the next state showed an 18-HP decline with no block remaining. The exact incoming damage is not inferable from the earlier DEBUG intent, but the state transition demonstrates that the aggressive opening failed to create a safe position.

title: Stop adding redundant attacks when the deck already has damage
situation: When a reward offers another copy of an attack already represented in the deck, particularly after HP has begun eroding, compare it against skipping and preserving draw quality or defensive density.
lesson: Prefer skipping redundant attack rewards unless the new copy fills a specific role. This run took a second Wild Strike and a second Pommel Strike, while the final 23-card deck remained attack-heavy; future runs should be more selective and value defensive or scaling cards when available.
evidence_points: At Act 1 Floor 8, Wild Strike was taken even though the final build contains two Wild Strikes.
At Act 2 Floor 21, Pommel Strike was taken even though the final build contains two Pommel Strikes, and skipping was an available alternative.
The final 23-card deck contains four Defends but repeated copies of Pommel Strike, Wild Strike, and Shockwave alongside many other attacks.
reasoning: The selections increased deck size and repetition without adding a new defensive function. This is not proof that either individual pick caused the loss, but the pattern made it harder to draw a survival-oriented hand in the final combat, where the opening hand had only defensive options that needed to be prioritized carefully.

title: At critical HP, take the guaranteed defense before attacking
situation: When HP is low, the enemy is attacking, and a defensive card is legal, especially on a turn where the fight is not already guaranteed to end.
lesson: Prioritize immediate block and survival over multi-card offense. In the Book of Stabbing fight, do not spend all available energy on attacks when a Defend is still legal; reassess whether preserving one more turn is more valuable than modest extra damage.
evidence_points: Turn 4 began at 14/72 HP with 4 energy, 0 block, and Book of Stabbing intending to attack; Defend was explicitly among the legal alternatives.
Instead, Uppercut, Shockwave, and Whirlwind+ were played, leaving 0 block before the enemy's attack.
reasoning: This is the strongest directly supported combat mistake: the final state presented a legal defensive action while the player was at lethal-risk HP, yet all energy was committed to offense. The run ended immediately after this sequence, so future decisions should first secure survival unless lethal damage is clearly established.

title: Stop adding attacks once the deck already has sufficient damage
situation: After obtaining several damage and scaling cards early, when later rewards offer more attacks alongside skip or utility options.
lesson: Become more selective with card rewards and skip mediocre attacks to preserve draw consistency. After acquiring Anger, Inflame, Whirlwind+, Sword Boomerang, Rampage, and other attacks, later rewards should be judged mainly by defensive value, draw, scaling, or essential utility rather than simply adding more damage.
evidence_points: The run repeatedly took attack cards including Anger, Whirlwind, Sword Boomerang, Rampage, Headbutt, Pummel, Carnage, Cleave+, and Clothesline+.
The final build contained 25 cards and remained heavily attack-oriented, including Heavy Blade, Whirlwind+, Sword Boomerang, Rampage, Carnage, Pummel, Cleave+, and Clothesline+.
reasoning: The trajectory shows a persistent pattern of accepting attack-heavy rewards, and the final deck confirms that these additions became permanent rather than temporary combat choices. A smaller, more selective deck would make key defensive cards and scaling pieces appear more reliably.

title: Treat Coffee Dripper as a commitment to preserving HP
situation: When selecting Coffee Dripper and entering the next act without a normal healing option at campfires.
lesson: After taking Coffee Dripper, avoid unnecessary chip damage and value defensive combat lines more highly; HP should be treated as a finite resource because routine campfire healing is no longer available.
evidence_points: The Act 1 boss reward chosen was Coffee Dripper, and it was the only boss relic selected.
After that choice, the Act 2 strategic log shows smithing at floor 23 but no rest action, while the run entered the final Book of Stabbing combat at 63/72 HP and fell to 14/72 during the fight.
reasoning: Coffee Dripper increases the cost of taking avoidable damage because the logged post-boss route does not show a later rest. The HP decline before and during the final combat supports using more conservative combat decisions once this relic is chosen.
